newsitem.title: FRANCE: Rebels kill 9, Algerian speaker condemns barbarity.
newsitem.headline: Rebels kill 9, Algerian speaker condemns barbarity.

text.p: Suspected Moslem guerrillas killed nine people, including a family of seven, at a fake roadblock in Algeria at the weekend, the Algerian newspaper Al Khabar said on Monday.
In another attack, a bomb wounded three people in the western city of Oran, the Algerian paper Le Matin said.

The violence, in which seven people had their throats cut, preceded a harsh denunciation of "terrorism" by Algeria's parliamentary speaker Abdelkader Bensalah who termed such acts a "shame for all humanity".
Bensalah, closing the first session of Algeria's first multi-party parliament on Monday, told MPs:

"How can we rest indifferent before the grief that our people have known during past years. And how can we keep silent in our anger before the barbarity of cowardly terrorist acts which are a shame for all humanity?"
The speaker said the session of parliament represented part of Algerians' victory over "terrorism" -- the official term for acts by Moslem fundamentalists seeking to overthrow the authorities.
"It is a victory of society over barbarity...The victory of life over death," he said in his speech reported by the official Algerian news agency APS.

The parliament, elected on June 5, is Algeria's first elected pluralist assembly. It follows a void of more than five years without an elected legislative body since the authorities scrapped the country's first multiparty parliamentary vote.

The authorities in January 1992 cancelled that first vote when Islamic fundamentalist took a huge lead in the first round. Violence erupted shortly afterwards and about 60,000 people have since been killed.
Since the June election, more than 700 people, including children and pregnant women, have been killed. Officials had said they hoped the ballot would see a start to ending the violence.
Around 300 rebels were also killed last month in a major military operation reported by Algerian newspapers.

Bensalah said he condemned "savage terrorist acts perpetrated against children, women and the men of this homeland". He reminded MPs of warnings abroad that governments should prepare to receive Algerian "boat people" fleeing the country, and of forecasts of the fall of the Algerian state.

"All this took place in concert with the strategy of terror and fear which our country knew and which was illustrated by widespread assassinations, fires, attacks and hangings with indescribable savagery," he said.
